texts.preamble: Ravinder Kumar And Others vs State Of Punjab And Others on 28 May, 2013 Author: Rajiv Narain Raina Bench: Rajiv Narain Raina Cwp No.20245 of 2012 -1- In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh ***** Cwp No.20245 of 2012 Date Of Decision :28.5.2013 Ravinder Kumar and others ...Petitioners Versus State of Punjab and others ...Respondents Coram:- Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajiv Narain Raina Present: Mr. Lalit Pathak, Advocate for the petitioners. Mr. T.N. Sarup, Addl. A.G. Punjab.
texts.facts: RAJIV NARAIN RAINA, J. The fourteen petitioners in this joint petition are Pan-Biri- Cigaretteewalas running their small businesses in Ludhiana of sale of tobacco and tobacco products including items like khaini, tobacco, Chaini Khaini and Zarda etc. The Government of Punjab in exercise of powers conferred under Section 30(2)(a) of the Food, Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions of Sales) Regulations, 2011 have issued notification dated 5.9.2012 prohibiting in the interest of public health sale of articles of food containing Tobacco and Nicotine as its ingredients being injurious to health. The petitioners aver that they have conformed to the notification and have stopped selling, distributing or storing Guthkas and Pan Masalas besides any article of food containing tobacco and nicotine as its ingredient; the ban though is specifically worded against Guthkas and Pan Masalas. However, while complying with the notification, they assert that the other items being sold through their shops do not fall under the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2002 and the Regulations framed thereunder. The expressions 'food' and 'primary food' have been defined in Section 3(j) and (2k). Regulation 2.3.4 prohibits sale of any food product which contains tobacco and nicotine. It is stated that the products like Khaini, Tobacco, Chaini-Khaini, Zarda etc do not form part of food when not mixed with food articles but are independent products which are either direct or refined form of Tobacco itself, therefore, is said to be not a food item, thus, not covered by the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2002. They complain that the respondents including the police and the officials of the Health Department at Ludhiana have started to interfere in the day-to-day business of the petitioners and are being harassed by misinterpreting the notification and extending its net to products which do not fall in the notification which bans manufacture, storage, sale or distribution of "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas" and any other food products containing tobacco and nicotine as ingredients. The life of this notification is for one year till 4/5.9.2013. In response to the writ petition, the State had filed a reply by way of affidavit of the Assistant Commissioner of Police (West) Ludhiana. A separate reply has been filed by the District Health Officer, Office of the Civil Surgeon Ludhiana by way of counter affidavit. In the police reply, it has been denied for want of knowledge that the petitioners have stopped selling the banned items. Harassment has been denied and it is stated that the local police have neither raided the shops of the petitioners nor any case has been registered against them nor have they been challaned so far. The health of people is paramount.
texts.arguments: "GOVERNMENT OF PUNJAB Office of the Commissioner Food Safety, Punjab State Institute of Health and Family Welfare Complex Phase VI Near Civil Hospital Ajitgarh (Mohali) Punjab No.11/10/12-3HB4/2584 Dated 5.9.2012 NOTIFICATION In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 30 (2) (a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2002006, and with provisions contained in Regulation 2,3,4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulation 2,3,4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations 2011, wherein prohibition in the interest of public health is to be ordered in the case of manufacture storage distribution or sale of any articles of food, having Tabacco and Nicotine as its ingredients being injurious to health. 2. Thus, the petitioners may be right in contending that when Tobacco and Nicotine when not used in production of food items, the ban may not run.
